articles.headline: Manchester United finally get Mauricio Pochettino after a decade of near misses
articles.description: After years of near misses and missed opportunities, Mauricio Pochettino is finally taking charge at Manchester United following a decade-long pursuit.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッド、10年にわたる後追いを経てついにマウリシオ・ポチェッティーノを招聘
articles.descriptionJa: 長年にわたる惜しい機会やチャンスを逃した末、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドは10年越しの追求を経て、ついにマウリシオ・ポチェッティーノを監督に迎える。
articles.body:
It feels a bit like destiny for Mauricio Pochettino to end up at Manchester United. After all, their flirtation with the former Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain and U.S. men's national team manager began more than 10 years ago.

In May 2016, amid mounting doubts over Louis van Gaal's future, Sir Alex Ferguson asked to meet Pochettino at a London restaurant. Jose Mourinho was already being lined up to replace Van Gaal, but Ferguson still asked the League Managers Association secretary for Pochettino's number.

The two-hour lunch at Scott's Restaurant in Mayfair would have stayed private, except the pair -- and Pochettino's assistant Jesus Perez -- were caught by paparazzi on the street outside.

Concerned about the speculation, Tottenham insisted it was just a "social occasion between colleagues." To quiet the noise further, they moved up an announcement that Pochettino had verbally agreed to a new five-year contract. Mourinho was confirmed as Van Gaal's successor weeks later.

United have made five permanent appointments since Pochettino's meeting with Ferguson and the former Argentina defender has never been far away.

When Mourinho was sacked in December 2018, Pochettino -- impressing at Spurs -- was considered the top choice for many Old Trafford executives. But with Pochettino under contract at Tottenham, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was given the caretaker role to steady the ship. Solskjaer won his first five games and in January 2019, United traveled to Spurs and won 1-0 to make it six from six.

Sources at United said there was no "defining moment" that decided Solskjaer would get the job permanently, but victory over Pochettino's Spurs was viewed as "a very positive sign." Two months later, Solskjaer signed a three-year deal; Pochettino was sacked by Tottenham in November 2019, five months after reaching the UEFA Champions League final.

Out of work and available, his name hung over Solskjaer's reign every time there was a blip. It reached the point in January 2021 that United bosses admitted they were "relieved" when Pochettino took over at Paris Saint-Germain. The feeling at the time was that the speculation had become a distraction and that Solskjaer would get more breathing space with Pochettino out of the picture as a potential replacement.

Solskjaer lasted another 11 months. When the Norwegian was sacked in November 2021, United opted for another caretaker in Ralf Rangnick and Pochettino was earmarked early on as a potential permanent appointment at the end of the season. It never materialized.

Form under Rangnick at the end of the 2021-22 season was so bad that United wanted to lift the mood and announce a permanent successor before the end of the campaign. In the end, it was a close call between Pochettino and Erik ten Hag. Crucially, Ajax allowed Ten Hag to negotiate with United during the season. articles.headline: Predicting how all 20 Premier League teams will finish the season
articles.description: After 10 games, we have enough data to predict every Premier League team's final spot in the standings for the 2026-27 season.
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグ全20チームのシーズン最終順位を予想
articles.descriptionJa: 10試合を終え、2026-27シーズンのプレミアリーグ全チームの最終順位を予想するための十分なデータが集まった。
articles.body:
At a glance, the Premier League table doesn't look that weird. The defending champs are in first, and Manchester City, Liverpool, and Chelsea all sit within the top five.

Except ... then there's Brighton in second place -- and not just that, but Brighton with a plus-19 goal differential. Or, put another way: Brighton with a goal differential that's better than Arsenal and Manchester City have combined to produce so far.

Oh, and then there's Everton -- who lost Iliman Ndiaye this summer and failed to sign a striker -- tied with Chelsea on points. Below them, there's Bournemouth, who lost their theoretically transformative manager, Andoni Iraola, to Liverpool. And below them, there's Brentford, who have a better goal differential than everyone in the league other than Brighton, Arsenal, and Man City.

Go further down the standings and Tottenham are in 11th, which is weird but what exact kind of weirdness is completely in the eye of the beholder. Two spots down from there, we've got Hull City, who were supposed to be one of the worst Premier League teams we've ever seen and who, through 10 games, have scored just as many goals as they've conceded.

None of the other promoted sides are in the bottom three, either. Instead, we've got a Europa League team in Crystal Palace anchoring the bottom, a Conference League team in Sunderland one spot ahead of them, and a Champions League team in Manchester United that is now managed by the guy who managed the U.S. men's national team this past summer.

And that's just the surface level. There's even more weirdness once you go a little deeper, like the fact that, say Nottingham Forest have attempted more shots than Arsenal, Liverpool, Man City, and Chelsea while also conceding the fewest shots of any team in the league. Or that, I don't know, Fulham have generated more touches in the opposition penalty area than anyone other than Man City or Arsenal?

With the financial rise of the Premier League's non-Big Six and the leaguewide trend toward man-marking and aggressive pressing, the things that have won soccer games in the past are not necessarily winning soccer games right now. And that makes it a little harder to predict what will win soccer games for the rest of the season.

However, we're 10 games into the current campaign -- a nice stopping point at which to ask ourselves: What will the Premier League table look like once we get to May?

How to predict the rest of the Premier League season

In the past, one of the easiest ways to predict the rest of the season was to just look at the Premier League table sorted by expected goals.

Obviously, it wouldn't tell you everything. But once you got to the 10-game mark, the best teams tended to be the teams that were creating more and better chances than their opponents.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Premier League clubs eye Cristiano Ronaldo successor Forbs
articles.description: Club Brugge winger Carlos Forbs is being tracked by a host of Premier League clubs after taking over the Portugal No. 7 shirt from Cristiano Ronaldo. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 【移籍噂・ニュース】プレミアリーグのクラブがクリスティアーノ・ロナウドの後継者フォルブスに注目
articles.descriptionJa: クルブ・ブルッヘのウィング、カルロス・フォルブスがクリスティアーノ・ロナウドからポルトガル代表の背番号7を引き継いだことで、多くのプレミアリーグクラブから注目されている。Transfer Talkが最新情報を伝える。
articles.body:
Club Brugge winger Carlos Forbs is being tracked by a host of Premier League clubs after taking over the Portugal No. 7 shirt from Cristiano Ronaldo, while Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite and Fulham's Calvin Bassey are among the options being considered by Manchester United. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- A host of Premier League clubs are keeping an eye on the situation of Club Brugge winger Carlos Forbs, says TEAMtalk. Forbs, 22, who recently took over the Portugal No. 7 shirt from Cristiano Ronaldo after he retired from international football, impressed in the win over Wales earlier this week. As a result, the likes of Aston Villa, Newcastle United, Brighton & Hove Albion, Everton and Brentford are looking to make a move before his potential transfer fee rises too much.

- Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite and Fulham's Calvin Bassey are among the options being considered by Manchester United as they aim to strengthen in defense, reports Sky Sports. The Red Devils are also continuing to monitor Fulham left back Antonee Robinson, who worked with Mauricio Pochettino with the USMNT, and could also revisit interest in Barcelona's Alejandro Balde. 

- Meanwhile, despite Juventus midfielder Weston McKennie claiming he doesn't want to leave the club, Gazzetta dello Sport insists that Pochettino still wants to reunite with the 28-year-old USMNT international at Old Trafford. Juve are looking to sign Marseille midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, but bringing in the 31-year-old could depend on what happens with McKennie and whether United make a €40 million offer to land him.

- Barcelona are looking at Internazionale's Alessandro Bastoni, Borussia Dortmund's Nico Schlotterbeck and Manchester United's Lisandro Martínez as they aim to sign a center back, as reported by Mundo Deportivo. The Blaugrana reached an agreement with Bastoni in the summer and though the deal fell through due to manager Hansi Flick prioritizing other areas, the 27-year-old remains open to a move. And the club have also renewed their efforts to sign Brighton's Luka Vuskovic, according to TEAMtalk. Vuskovic, 19, only joined the Seagulls in the summer from Spurs for £46 million, while Bayern Munich, Real Madrid and Liverpool are also monitoring the Croatia international's situation.

- AC Milan and Galatasaray have shown an interest in signing Manchester United attacking midfielder Bruno Fernandes as a free agent in July, as reported by Nicolo Schira. United have offered the 32-year-old a contract extension which would keep him at Old Trafford until 2029, but there is currently no agreement between the two parties. Fernandes turned down a large offer from Saudi Arabian side Al Hilal last June and is reportedly waiting for to see how Pochettino turns out before he commits himself.

articles.headline: Luka Doncic's shot goes cold as Jazz end Lakers' winning streak at 9
articles.description: Luka Doncic said his performance in Wednesday's loss to Utah, in which he shot 10-of-28 and had nine turnovers, was "unacceptable" as the Lakers' win streak ended at nine.
articles.headlineJa: ルカ・ドンチッチのシュートが決まらず、ジャズがレイカーズの9連勝に終止符
articles.descriptionJa: 水曜日のユタ戦で、28本中10本しか決められず9回のターンオーバーを記録したルカ・ドンチッチは、自身のパフォーマンスを「受け入れられない」と語った。これによりレイカーズの連勝は9で止まった。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- It was appropriate that the Lakers' thrilling overtime victory Tuesday felt like a party-like atmosphere at Crypto.com Arena, because as with most great parties, L.A. certainly paid for it the next day.

The Lakers' nine-game winning streak was snapped Wednesday in a 109-97 loss to the Jazz, with Utah separating itself down the stretch despite coming in near the bottom of the Western Conference standings.

The outcome lifted Utah to 3-13, good for 14th in the West. L.A. is now 13-3, still atop the conference.

But while the Lakers' late surge to topple the Charlotte Hornets on Tuesday showed resiliency while missing two of their starters in Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler, it was hard to tell which team was in first place and which team was the cellar dweller by how Wednesday's fourth quarter played out.

The Jazz outscored the Lakers 31-21, with Luka Doncic committing three of his nine turnovers.

"Honestly," Doncic said afterward, "I just got to do way better than this. This is unacceptable for my part. I got to lead the team in better ways."

It wasn't just that he personally coughed up the ball as many times as all of his teammates did combined. It was that when he shot it, he didn't connect nearly as often as he has been accustomed to in a start to the season that has already generated MVP buzz for the 27-year-old guard.

In Doncic's first 12 games, he averaged 39 points on 48.6% shooting, 40.6% from 3, 7.8 assists, 7.2 rebounds and 1.9 steals.

In his past two games in the back-to-back against Charlotte and Utah without Reaves, who is recovering from a bruised left heel, he averaged 32.5 points on 37.1% shooting, 25% from 3, 7.0 assists, 6.0 rebounds, 1.5 steals and 7.0 turnovers.

"I mean, the shot creation that is required from him, I think it takes its toll," Lakers coach JJ Redick said when asked about Doncic's energy level as L.A. played its third game in the past four days without Reaves. "That's the luxury of having two really elite creators, and obviously when they're both in the lineup, it makes things a little bit easier."

Doncic did not accept his coach's forgiveness for tired legs catching up to a star player shouldering the load during a packed stretch of the schedule.

"That can't be an excuse," Doncic said. "All NBA teams play 82 games, so that can't be an excuse."

Redick said before the game that Reaves progressed to an on-court workout for the first time since sustaining the foot injury last week in Milwaukee. His status for Friday's game against the Sacramento Kings is still to be determined.

Kessler's return Wednesday from a one-game absence because of soreness in his right leg didn't have much of an impact.

"It was a tough night for me," said Kessler, who finished with 10 points and 11 rebounds against his former team, but shot 3-for-7 from the field and 4-for-10 from the foul line. articles.headline: Ravens' Humphrey apologizes for quip that Baltimore 'best at making criminals'
articles.description: Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey apologized Wednesday for the derogatory comment he recently made about Baltimore on his podcast.
articles.headlineJa: レイブンズのハンフリー、ボルチモアを「犯罪者を作るのが一番上手い」と揶揄したことを謝罪
articles.descriptionJa: レイブンズのコーナーバック、マーロン・ハンフリーは水曜日、自身のポッドキャストでボルチモアに対して行った中傷的な発言について謝罪した。
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Outspoken Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey apologized for the derogatory comment he made about the city of Baltimore on his recent podcast.

On an episode of "The Marlon Humphrey Show" released Wednesday, Humphrey took a swipe at the city when asked what Baltimore was best at making.

After first mentioning "The Star-Spangled Banner" and National Bohemian beer, Humphrey quipped, "They're best at making criminals."

After Wednesday's practice, Humphrey said he regretted those remarks.

"I would like to apologize for some comments on my podcast I had to the city of Baltimore," Humphrey said. "As you guys know, I've been here my whole career. Spent lots of offseasons here. Welcomed a son here and I'm an investor in the city. And obviously, I do know the effect that words have and just like to apologize for those comments."

Humphrey received heavy fan backlash on social media Wednesday afternoon. The podcast episode featuring Humphrey's "criminals" comment has since been deleted from his YouTube page.

Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott acknowledged Humphrey's apology in a statement posted to social media, but noted, "a verbal apology is not enough. Baltimore is a city full of young Black boys who look to the Ravens as a beacon of light in their lives and to have someone that looks like them who wears a Baltimore Ravens jersey relegate them to becoming criminals cuts deeper. 

"I wonder how he would feel if prominent Baltimoreans used their platforms to imply that Baltimore once produced great defensive backs but we have recently lost our way."

Scott then added, "They wouldn't do that because our team and city are supposed to be united as one. Baltimore versus the world." 

Scott concluded his post by inviting Humphrey to sit down with him and some Baltimore citizens "who have re-entered into our community and are now preventing others from making the mistakes they made." 

Humphrey, 30, is in his 10th season with Baltimore and is the longest-tenured defensive player on the Ravens. The No. 16 selection in the 2017 draft by Baltimore, Humphrey has been to four Pro Bowls, which are the most by a Ravens cornerback.

In recent years, Humphrey has struggled and has drawn the ire of fans. This season, he has given up an NFL-worst 313 yards in coverage in the fourth quarter.

Asked if he understood why fans would be upset with this comment even if he was joking, Humphrey replied, "Yeah, I just apologized ... and that won't really happen again."

Humphrey is in the final year of a five-year, $97.5 million extension. His $26.276 million salary cap hit is the largest for any cornerback in 2026.

Humphrey's slight at Baltimore comes at a time when the franchise is dealing with one of its worst stretches in its history. The Ravens (4-6) have lost five straight, including a 23-20 loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers on Monday. Baltimore has also lost seven of its past eight games at home.

articles.headline: Florio, Simms apologize for comments about Vrabel's mustache in Germany
articles.description: "PFT Live" hosts Mike Florio and Chris Simms apologized for comments they made about Mike Vrabel's mustache when talking about the Patriots' trip to Germany.
articles.headlineJa: フロリオとシムズ、ドイツでのヴラベルの口髭に関する発言を謝罪
articles.descriptionJa: 「PFT Live」のホストであるマイク・フロリオとクリス・シムズは、パトリオッツのドイツ遠征について話す際に、マイク・ヴラベルの口髭に関して行った発言を謝罪した。
articles.body:
Mike Florio and Chris Simms, hosts of the "PFT Live" podcast, apologized for comments they made on a recent episode about New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel's mustache during the team's recent trip to Germany.

Florio, responding to Simms saying Vrabel has a "German mustache," said "you have to be careful trimming that thing" in an apparent allusion to Adolf Hitler's mustache before defending the comment saying "it's funny ... it was 80 years ago, let's have some fun for crying out loud." 

While apparently alluding to Hitler, neither host said his name. 

"On yesterday's (Nov. 17) PFT Live show, we made comments that some found offensive and we apologize," Florio and Simms said in a statement released by NBC Sports on Wednesday. 

Jeff Miller, the NFL's executive vice president of communications and public affairs, said in a statement: "We found the remarks inappropriate and offensive."

articles.headline: Niners' Nick Bosa on 4-game sack drought: 'Don't think I'm playing my best'
articles.description: Niners star Nick Bosa acknowledged his performance this season, including four straight games with no sacks, hasn't been up to his usual standard.
articles.headlineJa: ナイナーズのニック・ボサ、4試合連続サックなしについて：「最高のプレーができているとは思わない」
articles.descriptionJa: ナイナーズのスター、ニック・ボサは、4試合連続サックなしを含む今シーズンのパフォーマンスが、自身の通常水準に達していないことを認めた。
articles.body:
COLORADO SPRINGS, Colo. -- After failing to record a sack in his fourth straight game, San Francisco 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa acknowledged Wednesday that his performance this season has not been up to his usual standard.

In the Niners' 46-40 win against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, Bosa played 34 defensive snaps in which he had a pass rush opportunity. He finished with no sacks, one quarterback hit and four pressures while also being called for three penalties, including two for jumping offside.

It's the first time since Bosa entered the league in 2019 that he hasn't had a sack in four straight games in the same season.

"I think in the past when I was younger, it would eat at me a lot more, just strictly the stat aspects," Bosa said after the Niners completed their first practice of the week at the Air Force Academy in preparation for this week's showdown with the Minnesota Vikings. "But now I'm really just focused on the people around me, and if I feel like I'm playing good football, then I really don't care much about the stats. But I don't think I'm playing my best football right now. So that's what gets to me more so than the actual stats."

Bosa is still working his way back from multiple injuries. He missed all but three games in 2025 because of a torn ACL in his right knee. During training camp this year, Bosa participated in individual drills in the opening days but then missed most of the preseason before playing 70 snaps in the first two games of the season.

But before the Niners played the Arizona Cardinals in Week 3, Bosa strained his calf while warming up during a Thursday walkthrough and missed the ensuing five games. Bosa said that injury was a result of overcompensation from his ACL recovery.

Upon returning, Bosa has attempted to fit into new coordinator Raheem Morris' defensive scheme. The system isn't drastically different from what Bosa and other veteran Niners have played in, but has enough nuance that it takes some time to catch up.

Bosa said Wednesday that he also could have done a better job being proactive about learning those details about Morris' defense.

"I think there's a learning curve and ... a lot of guys haven't had many reps in the scheme so far," Bosa said. "I'm trying to break it down to the basics and just kind of get back. I missed a year and then missed camp. I kind of took for granted some of the things that I did automatically, and I thought I could just kind of coast and continue to do those things automatically and focus on other things. But I need to, especially with a newer defense, really hone in on the things that made me the player that I am."

Asked for an example of something he needs to refocus on, Bosa pointed to doing a better job of setting his feet and getting off the ball at the snap, before stopping short of sharing too much for competitive reasons.

"It takes time," Bosa said. "I'm not going to make excuses because nobody really cares. But I'm going to get better and I'm pretty

articles.headline: TNF: Texans rule out DE Hunter, RB Marks; Colts rule out CB Ward, starting OTs
articles.description: The Texans and Colts ruled out several key contributors for their Thursday night matchup.
articles.headlineJa: 木曜夜の試合（TNF）：テキサンズはDEハンターとRBマークスを欠場、コルツはCBウォードと先発OTを欠場
articles.descriptionJa: テキサンズとコルツは、木曜夜の対戦に向けて、複数の主力選手を欠場させると発表した。
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- Key players for the Houston Texans and the Indianapolis Colts will be out for their AFC South matchup on "Thursday Night Football."

For the Texans, All-Pro defensive end Danielle Hunter is out with a hamstring injury after missing Houston's Week 10 loss to the Cleveland Browns, where they blew a 17-0 lead. That comes on the heels of Pro Bowl linebacker and team leader in tackles Azeez Al-Shaair being placed on injured reserve with a groin injury.

On the offensive side, the Texans will be without running back Woody Marks, who sustained a concussion on a second-down carry in the third quarter against the Browns. Browns defenders Emmanuel McNeil-Warren, Sam Kamara and Quincy Williams collided with Marks, leaving him on the ground for a few minutes.

A potential replacement for Marks is David Montgomery, but he has been out since Week 4 (groin). Montgomery practiced last week, and on Tuesday he said he's "trending in the right direction." He has no injury designation for the game.

Wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. is also out with a hamstring for the second straight game.

On the Colts' side, they will be without Pro Bowl starting cornerback Charvarius Ward, who sustained a knee injury in Sunday's win over the Miami Dolphins and did not practice this week.

Indianapolis also will be missing both starting tackles, a concerning development considering the impact that Houston defensive end Will Anderson Jr. had in the teams' first meeting in September. Left tackle Bernhard Raimann is still being treated for a concussion, and right tackle Jalen Travis will miss his second consecutive game with a knee injury. Tight end Will Mallory will not play because of a hamstring injury.

In the Colts' Week 3 win over Houston, Anderson dominated Indianapolis with 2.5 sacks, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. He matched a career high with eight pressures in the game.

Cornerback Sauce Gardner, who has been dealing with calf issues off and on since last season, aggravated the injury Sunday and is listed as questionable. Another injury of note is the toe issue that has slowed receiver Anthony Gould. He took over the starting role in the slot after Josh Downs was traded to the Kansas City Chiefs earlier this month. Gould is listed as questionable.

articles.headline: Giants RB Cam Skattebo to nix backflips in wake of Aidan Hutchinson's injury
articles.description: Giants RB Cam Skattebo said he is holding off on doing any more backflips after Lions DE Aidan Hutchinson suffered a major knee injury while leaping and celebrating a sack.
articles.headlineJa: ジャイアンツのRBカム・スカテボ、エイダン・ハッチンソンの怪我を受けてバックフリップを中止へ
articles.descriptionJa: ジャイアンツのRBカム・スカテボは、ライオンズのDEエイダン・ハッチンソンがサックを祝って跳ね上がった際に膝の重傷を負ったことを受け、今後バックフリップを行うことは控えると語った。
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is retiring his trademark celebratory backflip for the time being.

This comes on the heels of Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson suffering a season-ending knee injury while leaping and celebrating a sack Sunday. Hutchinson was placed on injured reserve.

"It's hard to see," Skattebo told reporters Wednesday. "I'm saying, yeah, [no backflips]. Mentally, I'm like, 'I'm not doing that.'

"That s--- ain't going to happen to me."

Skattebo, the Giants starting running back, is coming off a serious ankle injury last year. But he returned for the start of the season and backflipped after scoring in New York's season-opening win over the Dallas Cowboys. He backflipped as recently as Thursday night in a loss to the Washington Commanders.

 

Skattebo isn't saying he won't backflip again. The likelihood is he will. He has done it his whole life. But he mentioned after the opener that he might put the celebration on the backburner, before it reemerged in Week 10.

Skattebo conceded Wednesday the backflip might resurface "if we go to the playoffs or something."

The backflip was a point of contention throughout the offseason, even before Hutchinson had his mishap. Skattebo did his flip for the first time since the injury after hitting a home run at the Brian Burns Celebrity Softball Game in late May.

Skattebo then stumbled while doing a backflip at Fanatics Fest over the summer, creating a stir.

Giants brass had a conversation with Skattebo afterward. They preferred he didn't do it leading into the season, especially coming off a major injury. They didn't mandate he never do it again.

"The big-picture message is you want to take care of yourself, take care of your team. Do everything you can do to be healthy, be back, be right, be good," Giants coach John Harbaugh said at the start of training camp. "What does that mean? It's not going to be the same situation the next time for anybody. It's going to be different. So, it's really the principle of it."

Skattebo, 24, leads the Giants with 496 yards rushing and four touchdowns on 116 carries so far this season.

Hutchinson, 26, isn't the first player to be injured while celebrating. Former Arizona Cardinals kicker Bill Gramatica tore his ACL while celebrating a made kick against the Giants in 2001. But the current Hutchinson situation has prompted some debate about whether coaches should talk to players about celebrations, potentially banning anything that could be deemed dangerous.

"No, I don't believe that," Lions coach Dan Campbell said. "I think what happened speaks for itself. We're not talking to 8-year-olds here."

articles.headline: Panthers secondary set for boost with return of CB Mike Jackson
articles.description: Panthers starting cornerback Mike Jackson, who has been sidelined since injuring his groin in Week 3, plans to be in the lineup Sunday against the Ravens.
articles.headlineJa: CBマイク・ジャクソンの復帰により、パンサーズのセカンダリーが強化へ
articles.descriptionJa: 第3週に鼠径部の負傷で離脱していたパンサーズの先発コーナーバック、マイク・ジャクソンが、日曜日のレイブンズ戦でラインナップに復帰する予定だ。
articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Carolina Panthers starting cornerback Mike Jackson (groin) plans to be in the lineup Sunday against the Baltimore Ravens at Bank of America Stadium.

"I'm game ready, so I'll be out there on Sunday," Jackson said after Wednesday's practice.

Jackson had his 21-day practice window opened last week, but he didn't play in Carolina's 20-17 win over the New Orleans Saints.

The 29-year-old cornerback was a full participant in the first workout of Week 11, and coach Dave Canales noted that Jackson and running back Jonathon Brooks (groin) were on the cusp of returning from injured reserve.

"I think they're ready," Canales said. "We do have to work through all the different things with the roster ... so that's the part that [general manager] Dan [Morgan] and I have to talk about, but these guys are hungry to get back out there and so we're going to try to find a way for them to help us."

Brooks underwent core muscle surgery after leaving the Panthers' Week 2 win over the Falcons with a groin injury. Brooks has played in just five of 43 regular season-games since being selected with the 46th pick in the 2024 NFL draft. During his two games this season, Brooks collected 30 rushing yards and 43 receiving yards on 11 total touches. He's yet to score his first NFL touchdown in his limited action.

Jackson injured his groin in a Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns and underwent surgery the following week. Jackson and fellow starting cornerback Jaycee Horn (quad), who was also injured against the Browns, have missed the Panthers' past six games.

Rookie Will Lee III, Chau Smith-Wade and practice squad call-ups Marco Wilson and Corey Thornton have played in place of the injured starting cornerbacks as the Panthers have gone 3-3 in their absence. Lee, who has missed the past two weeks with a left hamstring injury, was a full participant Wednesday and Canales said he expected the rookie to play in Week 11 as well.

And while Lee has flashed during his rookie season, Jackson's return should provide a proven boost to the secondary. Jackson led the NFL with 19 pass breakups last season. He has also produced six interceptions during his 37 games with the Panthers.

"On Sundays, knowing that you have a guy like that out there, it's huge," quarterback Bryce Young said.

The Panthers are also weighing the status of versatile offensive lineman Brady Christensen.

The 2021 third-round pick had his 21-day practice window opened in Week 9 and the Panthers have until Tuesday of next week to activate him onto the 53-man roster.

If Carolina does not activate Christensen before the deadline, he will revert back to season-ending injured reserve.

"Brady is ready to go, too," Canales said. "And again, it's just a matter of timing, space on the roster and all those things, and we're up against it now with Brady, with his window being open."

articles.headline: How fallen giants and their fans bounce back from scandal, relegation
articles.description: Some of Europe's greatest teams have suffered relegation as punishment. So what might lie ahead for Man City?
articles.headlineJa: 没落した名門クラブとファンは、いかにしてスキャンダルや降格から立ち直るのか
articles.descriptionJa: 欧州の偉大なチームの中には、罰則として降格を経験したチームもある。マンチェスター・シティには何が待ち受けているのだろうか。
articles.body:
What does it feel like to realize the club you love is stuck in a doom spiral of its own making?

Whether due to cheating, financial mismanagement or general ineptitude, some of Europe's greatest teams have suffered the ignominy of relegation by means of punishment -- and their supporters have watched it unfold. From Juventus and Fiorentina in Italy to Rangers in Scotland, fans have seen offices stripped bare and managers and players scrambling for places on the first boats off the sinking ship.

But a crisis offers the chance for heroes to drag their team out of the deep while suits swap seats in the boardrooms. And amid schadenfreude, anger and denial, supporters of flawed giants find unity through their morbid, self-deprecating humor and fortitude in their situation.

As Manchester City's fans await the results of their appeal and the level of punishment for their 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules, they might find some small comfort in seeing how others have bounced back from the depths of despair ... or renewed dread at the tribulations that could lie ahead.

Fleeing for greener pastures

By the time manager Fabio Capello had sprinted to Real Madrid in 2006, taking stars Emerson and Fabio Cannavaro with him, Juventus' offices had already been ransacked.

The "Calciopoli" scandal started as a doping investigation into Juventus, but instead found evidence of attempted match-fixing by executives who manipulated referees and their bosses -- a scandal that also implicated Fiorentina, AC Milan, Reggina and Lazio. Papers, contracts and hard drives were seized by the Guardia di Finanza (Financial Police) on May 18, 2006.

The original swath of punishments was handed out just six days after Italy won the 2006 World Cup. Juventus were hammered the hardest; they were kicked down to Serie B and stripped of their 2005 and 2006 league titles, triggering a flurry of expedited exit strategies.

"This world had been turned upside down," Ibrahimovic wrote in his 2011 autobiography. "It wasn't possible to take it all in. We'd won two titles in a row -- were we going to lose everything? One after one the players got away ... every one of us who were left called our agents: 'Sell us, sell us.'

"Uncertainty and desperation hung in the air ... No way was I going to sacrifice a year in the second division. My best years were in danger of being wasted; I told [agent Mino Raiola], 'Do whatever it takes, just get me out of here.'"

Ibrahimovic watched teammates Lilian Thuram and Gianluca Zambrotta join Barcelona, while Patrick Vieira headed to Internazionale. Didier Deschamps took charge, though he couldn't persuade Ibrahimovic to stay. Ibrahimovic said he'd train but wouldn't play in matches, leading to the striker refusing to get on the bus for a preseason game -- instead, he hid in his room and played video games, eventually joining Vieira at Inter.

articles.headline: Mauricio Pochettino arrives at Man United: 'You will see, give me time'
articles.description: Mauricio Pochettino arrived at Manchester United for his first day as head coach on Wednesday but said he requires "time" to turn the club's fortunes around.
articles.headlineJa: マウリシオ・ポチェッティーノがマン・ユナイテッドに就任：「見ていてくれ、時間をくれ」
articles.descriptionJa: マウリシオ・ポチェッティーノは水曜日、ヘッドコーチとしての初日でマンチェスター・ユナイテッドに到着したが、クラブの運命を変えるには「時間」が必要だと語った。
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino arrived at Manchester United for his first day as head coach on Wednesday but said he requires "time" to turn the club's fortunes around.

Pochettino's final act in charge of the United States national side was a 2-0 victory over Haiti in Cincinnati on Tuesday night.

A plane carrying Pochettino arrived at Manchester Airport on Wednesday afternoon. He headed to the club's training ground, Carrington, as the replacement for the sacked Michael Carrick before his first game leading United on Sunday against Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League.

On Tuesday night, Pochettino was told by former Manchester City and United States player DaMarcus Beasley that "Manchester is blue, it will always be blue."

He responded: "You will see. Give me time.

"The new challenge is a big challenge, but at the same time it's adrenalin you want to feel. We need to add our common sense... we know the situation is not a situation that deserves to be a club like Manchester United, the fan base is amazing."

Pochettino added: "The mentality is to learn from everyone. You need to have an open mind because I think the players can teach us every day, we are much better coaching staff now.

"Football is about attitude, and it's about the approach. It's about connection, feelings and communication."

Upon arrival at Carrington, Pochettino said he is "very excited to be here. It's an honour. It's a privilege to be in this amazing club. Yes, looking forward to start to work."

United have confirmed Jesus Perez, Miguel D'Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino as Pochettino's staff. 

Mauricio Pochettino starts work at Man United on Wednesday

Pochettino was also asked about whether he can improve United's running statistics, which were criticised by ex-boss Carrick after a drab 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League.

In response to Bruno Fernandes' questioning of the team's tactics, Carrick said: "Whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you ain't going to win."

Pochettino said on Tuesday night: "What I can talk in general, football is very complex and I think it's not important if you run or not run.

"You need to run well, you need to run with an objective, you need to run together. Then you need to play, you need to know what you need to do, you need to express your talent. The mindsets are so important."

Pochettino led the U.S. to the round of 16 at last summer's World Cup on home soil.

But he is now returning to the Premier League where he has previously coached Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea.
